name: Sui din
summary: Sủi dìn is a soft, chewy winter dumpling of wet-milled glutinous rice, filled with shredded coconut, sesame, and peanuts. The ginger syrup is hot enough to burn the tongue.
origin: Hai Phong. The city portal on 23 December 2012, and again as a city mark on 16 October 2025.
texture: The 2012 account says the dough is soft and chewy when the glutinous rice is wet-milled.
taste: Ginger hot enough to burn the tongue, with a fatty coconut, sesame, and peanut filling. The syrup is fresh ginger cooked with nước đường hoa mai. The account says the sweetness is not the sweetness of chè.
howToEat: Eat it in winter, from a pot at the edge of an alley.
A price was not printed. The hour is Check on arrival.
where: The 2012 account says any alley in the city, not one street. The hour is Check on arrival.
seoTitle: Sui din — Hai Phong’s winter ginger dumpling
seoDescription: A winter glutinous-rice dumpling of coconut, sesame, and peanut in a ginger syrup hot enough to burn the tongue.
